messages.subject: Request to adding some parameters for more handy and beautiful data visualization
messages.subject_clean: Request to adding some parameters for more handy and beautiful data visualization
messages.body_plain:
Dear Zhian,

I'm a poppr user and it's really powerful and flexible to my polyploidy data set. I noticed that your development group has contributed lots of efforts to the data visualization and its effect is pretty good based on my use experience. However, I guess it will become more handy and powerful if you would like to add some parameters, for example, font sizes, styles or colors in your default setting of parameters for data visualization. So could you post some codes for these effects of visualization?

Thanks,
Jianan

messages.subject: recode.polyploids for DAPC
messages.body_plain: Hello. I have a set of microsatellite data for an hexaploid. I wanted to use adegenet and found that poppr had a very easy way to input data. I uploaded my data using poppr method and as a data frame though when i uploaded my data I found and extra allele in all loci. I have read that poppr can fix it using the command recode.polyploids. I want to do DAPC using my data but I believe this analysis is related to allele frequencies, should I use recode.polyploids before continuing or letting them as they are? adegenet tutorial doesn't take this into consideration.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jianan,

I apologize for not replying to this sooner. I will post a tutorial on this soon. As far as giving specific options in the functions for the customization of fonts and other aspects, I will consider it. There are, however many permutations of possibilities regarding visualization customization where it becomes challenging on the programming side when factors like fonts (not standardized across systems) come into play. Since many of the plots in poppr are ggplot2 plots, they can be manipulated in R after the fact. In section 4.2 of the poppr manual <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/poppr/vignettes/poppr_manual.pdf>, there are basic instructions on how to manipulate these graphics. Again, I will post a tutorial soon on this subject.

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: recode.polyploids for DAPC
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Short answer:

Yes, you should use recode_polyploids. It would also be valuable to do the DAPC analysis without. It is also important to make sure that your analyses are not clustering relative to the observed ploidy.

Long answer:

The extra allele in your data is the "0" used to code missing data for polyploids. This is a way to trick the genind object into thinking that ploidy is constant over the entire data set. As documented in the recode_polyploids help documentation and section 1.12 of the poppr manual <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/poppr/vignettes/poppr_manual.pdf>, this method works well with the index of association, Bruvo's distance, and mlg functions as these know to ignore the zeroes. The frequency-based statistics will consider zeroes as an allele, which is why you will have a heterozygosity of 1 across all loci when you analyze the summary statistics of your genind object. The function recode_polyploids will remove the zeroes and will recode the frequencies of alleles so that each allele has an equal probability of being observed. This is not a perfect solution as it does not account for partial heterzygotes and will consider a genotype with the alleles A and B to be A/A/A/B/B/B even if in reality it's A/A/A/A/A/B. You will want to run the analysis with and without correction for polyploids to see if there is any effect on the data.

I hope that helps.

Cheers,
Zhian
